previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, GERD, and prior Puestow procedure was admitted for a four-day history of worsening left lower quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting, with inability to tolerate oral intake. Initial CT showed stable chronic pancreatitis without acute findings, and labs supported a non-acute etiology. He was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and a Dilaudid PCA for pain control. His symptoms improved over several days, allowing advancement to a full diet and transition to oral pain medication. GERD was addressed with continuation of omeprazole and discontinuation of ranitidine following EGD-confirmed Grade C esophagitis. Diarrhea resolved during admission. He was discharged home with a one-week supply of oral Dilaudid, instructions to use Miralax and senna for constipation, and a plan to follow up with his primary care provider for long-term pain management, including consideration of Suboxone. An IgG subclass test was ordered to evaluate for autoimmune pancreatitis.
